This Advent, look for someone who might be lonely: a widow, a neighbor, a shut-in. You can be a small picture of Immanuel by showing up, calling, or sending a card. God came near to us; we can come near to others.
2026-12-12.prayer: Immanuel, thank You that You are with me always. Let me be a sign of Your presence to someone who feels alone today. Amen.
2026-12-12.title: Immanuel
2026-12-12.today: Call or visit someone who may be lonely this season.

2026-12-13.verse: The Word became flesh, and lived among us. We saw his glory, such glory as of the one and only Son of the Father, full of grace and truth.
2026-12-13.reflection:
John's Gospel doesn't start with shepherds or a manger. It starts before time itself: In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God. Through Him all things were made.

Then comes the most astonishing sentence in the Bible: The Word became flesh, and lived among us.

The Creator of galaxies became an embryo. The One who spoke the oceans into being was bathed by His mother. The eternal Son learned to walk, got tired, felt hunger, and wept at a friend's grave.

The word translated lived among us literally means pitched His tent. It recalls the tabernacle in the wilderness, where God's glory dwelt among Israel. Now God's glory dwells in a Person.

John says we saw His glory, full of grace and truth. Not grace without truth, which would excuse everything. Not truth without grace, which would condemn us. But both, perfectly, in Jesus.

This is why Christmas matters. God didn't just tell us about Himself. He showed us.
2026-12-13.prayer: Lord Jesus, eternal Word, thank You for becoming flesh and living among us. Let me behold Your glory, full of grace and truth. Amen.
2026-12-13.title: The Word Became Flesh
2026-12-13.today: Read John 1:1-14 slowly today, and marvel at the wonder of the incarnation.

2026-12-14.verse: The light shines in the darkness, and the darkness hasn’t overcome it.
2026-12-14.reflection:
December has the shortest days of the year. Darkness comes early and stays late. It's no wonder Christians have long lit candles during Advent, each week adding another flame as Christmas approaches.

John writes, The light shines in the darkness, and the darkness hasn't overcome it. The verb is present tense: the light keeps shining. It hasn't gone out, and it never will.

John was writing about Jesus, the true light that gives light to everyone. The darkness tried its best to put Him out. It nailed Him to a cross and sealed Him in a tomb. But on the third day, the light rose again.

Whatever darkness we see in the world, or feel in our own hearts, it does not get the final word. One candle is enough to push back the dark in a whole room.

Jesus also told His followers, You are the light of the world. We carry His light into dark places through kindness, prayer, and faithful witness.

Let His light shine through you today.
2026-12-14.prayer: Lord Jesus, light of the world, thank You that the darkness cannot overcome You. Shine in my heart, and through me into the lives of others. Amen.
2026-12-14.title: The Light Shines in the Darkness
2026-12-14.today: Light a candle this evening and pray for someone who is in a dark season.

2026-12-15.verse: But when the fullness of the time came, God sent out his Son, born to a woman, born under the law, that he might redeem those who were under the law, that we might receive the adoption of children.
2026-12-15.reflection:
From the garden of Eden onward, God had promised a Redeemer. Generations came and went. Abraham, Moses, David, and the prophets all looked forward to Him. Then came four hundred years of silence between the Old and New Testaments, with no new prophet and no word from heaven.

But God had not forgotten. Paul writes that when the fullness of the time came, God sent out His Son, born to a woman, born under the law, to redeem those who were under the law, that we might receive adoption as children.

Historians point out how ready the world was: Roman roads connected nations, a common Greek language carried the gospel, and the hopes of Israel were burning. God's timing was perfect.

His timing in our lives is perfect, too, even when it feels slow. Prayers we've prayed for decades are not forgotten.

And notice the purpose: adoption. Jesus came not just to forgive us, but to bring us into God's family as beloved sons and daughters. That is the heart of Christmas.
2026-12-15.prayer: Father, thank You for sending Your Son at just the right time, and for adopting me into Your family. I trust Your timing in my life. Amen.
2026-12-15.title: The Fullness of Time
2026-12-15.today: Thank God today for a prayer He answered in His perfect timing, even if it took years.

2026-12-16.verse: The people who walked in darkness have seen a great light. Those who lived in the land of the shadow of death, on them the light has shined.
2026-12-16.reflection:
During World War II, London enforced a nightly blackout. Every window was covered, every streetlight dark, so enemy bombers couldn't find their targets. People who lived through it remembered the joy when the lights finally came back on after the war.

Isaiah spoke to people living in a kind of blackout. The northern regions of Israel, Zebulun and Naphtali, had been the first to fall to Assyrian invaders. They knew deep darkness. To them God promised: The people who walked in darkness have seen a great light.

Seven hundred years later, Jesus began His ministry in exactly that region, around the Sea of Galilee. Matthew tells us it was to fulfill this very prophecy. The light came first to the places that had been darkest longest.

That's how God works. He goes to the hardest places first. If you are in a season of darkness, grief, or worry, Christ's light is especially for you.

The great light has dawned. The blackout is over for all who come to Him.
2026-12-16.prayer: Lord, thank You for the great light of Jesus. Shine on me and on all who walk in darkness. Let Your light reach the hardest places. Amen.
2026-12-16.title: A Great Light
2026-12-16.today: Pray today for a place in the world that is experiencing deep darkness.

2026-12-17.verse: A shoot will come out of the stock of Jesse, and a branch out of his roots will bear fruit. Yahweh’s Spirit will rest on him: the spirit of wisdom and understanding, the spirit of counsel and might, the spirit of knowledge and of the fear of Yahweh.
2026-12-17.reflection:
Anyone who has cut down a tree knows that sometimes, months later, a small green shoot appears from the stump. What looked dead was still alive underneath.

Isaiah used that picture to describe the family of King David. By Isaiah's time, the royal line was in decline, and eventually it would be cut down entirely when Babylon conquered Jerusalem. It looked like the end.

But God promised: A shoot will come out of the stock of Jesse, and a branch out of his roots will bear fruit. The Spirit of the Lord would rest on Him, the Spirit of wisdom and understanding, counsel and might, knowledge and the fear of the Lord.

That Branch was Jesus, born of David's line in a time when David's family were simple carpenters.

Maybe there's an area of your life that feels cut down: a dream that died, a relationship that ended, a body that's failing. God specializes in new life from stumps. The resurrection proves it. With Him, what looks like an ending can become a beginning.
2026-12-17.prayer: Lord, thank You that You bring new life from what seems dead. Fill me with hope in Jesus, the Branch from Jesse's root. Amen.
2026-12-17.title: A Shoot from the Stump
2026-12-17.today: Bring God one area of your life that feels dead, and ask Him to bring new life there.

2026-12-18.verse: Joseph also went up from Galilee, out of the city of Nazareth, into Judea, to David’s city, which is called Bethlehem, because he was of the house and family of David; to enroll himself with Mary, who was pledged to be married to him as wife, being pregnant.
2026-12-18.reflection:
Caesar Augustus, sitting in Rome, issued a decree that everyone should be registered for a census. He had no idea he was fulfilling a prophecy. Because of his order, Joseph took Mary, heavily pregnant, on the long journey from Nazareth to Bethlehem, about ninety miles over hills and rough roads.

It must have been exhausting and uncomfortable. They didn't know where they would stay. Yet through their ordinary obedience to an ordinary government order, God brought the Messiah to be born in the very town Micah had named centuries before.

God was quietly directing even an emperor's paperwork to accomplish His purposes.

Most of our lives are made up of ordinary steps: appointments, errands, chores, and obligations. It's easy to think they don't matter much. But God weaves His plans through just such steps.

Joseph and Mary didn't see the big picture as they walked. They just kept going, one mile at a time, trusting God. We can do the same. He is working in the ordinary road you're walking today.
2026-12-18.prayer: Lord, thank You that You work through ordinary steps. Help me be faithful today in small things, trusting Your bigger plan. In Jesus' name, Amen.
2026-12-18.title: The Journey to Bethlehem
2026-12-18.today: As you go about an ordinary task today, offer it to God as an act of faithfulness.

2026-12-19.verse: She gave birth to her firstborn son. She wrapped him in bands of cloth, and laid him in a feeding trough, because there was no room for them in the inn.
2026-12-19.reflection:
Luke tells the story simply: Mary gave birth to her firstborn son, wrapped Him in strips of cloth, and laid Him in a manger, because there was no room for them in the inn.

A manger is a feeding trough for animals. The King of kings spent His first night on earth in a place that smelled of hay and livestock. No palace, no royal nursery, no crowd of attendants.

From the very beginning, Jesus identified with the poor, the overlooked, and the crowded-out. He would later say that foxes have holes and birds have nests, but the Son of Man has nowhere to lay His head.

The phrase no room has often been applied to our own hearts. It's easy to fill our lives so full, even with good things, that there's no space left for Jesus. Especially at Christmas, the busyness can crowd Him out.

But He still comes humbly. He doesn't force His way in. He waits to be welcomed. Make room for Him today, in your schedule and in your heart.
2026-12-19.prayer: Lord Jesus, I make room for You in my heart. Thank You for coming so humbly. Help me welcome You above all else this Christmas. Amen.
2026-12-19.title: No Room in the Inn
2026-12-19.today: Set aside fifteen minutes today to sit quietly with Jesus amid the holiday busyness.

2026-12-20.verse: There were shepherds in the same country staying in the field, and keeping watch by night over their flock. Behold, an angel of the Lord stood by them, and the glory of the Lord shone around them, and they were terrified.
2026-12-20.reflection:
In Jesus' day, shepherds were near the bottom of the social ladder. Their work kept them outdoors, away from the temple, and many people looked down on them. Their testimony wasn't even accepted in court.

Yet when God announced the birth of His Son, He didn't send the angel to the palace in Jerusalem or the high priest's house. He sent the angel to shepherds, keeping watch over their flocks by night outside Bethlehem.

Suddenly an angel stood before them, and the glory of the Lord shone around them, and they were terrified.

There's a lovely fittingness here. These shepherds may have been raising lambs for temple sacrifices. Now they were being told about the Lamb of God who would take away the sin of the world. And Jesus would grow up to call Himself the Good Shepherd.

God still delights in revealing Himself to humble, ordinary people doing their ordinary work. You don't need status or a title to meet Jesus. You just need a willing heart.
2026-12-20.prayer: Lord, thank You for revealing Your glory to humble hearts. Let me see Your glory today in the middle of my ordinary life. Amen.
2026-12-20.title: Shepherds in the Field
2026-12-20.today: As you do your ordinary work today, remember God sees you just as He saw those shepherds.

2026-12-21.verse: The angel said to them, “Don’t be afraid, for behold, I bring you good news of great joy which will be to all the people.
2026-12-21.reflection:
The shepherds were trembling with fear when the angel spoke: Don't be afraid, for behold, I bring you good news of great joy which will be to all the people.

Good news. In a world full of bad news, then as now, God's announcement was different. It wasn't a warning or a command. It was news, something that had happened, something God had done.

Great joy. Not mild pleasure, not passing happiness, but deep, overflowing joy.

To all the people. Not just the religious elite, not just Israel, but everyone. Rich and poor, young and old, near and far.

Many of us grew up hearing these words every Christmas, perhaps from Linus in A Charlie Brown Christmas, quoting the King James Version on a quiet stage. They never grow old.

The joy of Christmas isn't about getting everything right: the perfect gifts, the perfect meal, the perfect family gathering. It's about what God has done in sending a Savior. That joy is available even in grief, even in loneliness, even in illness. It is good news, and it is for you.
2026-12-21.prayer: Lord, thank You for the good news of great joy. Fill my heart with Christmas joy that doesn't depend on circumstances, and help me share it. Amen.
2026-12-21.title: Good News of Great Joy
2026-12-21.today: Share the good news of Christmas with someone today, through a card, call, or conversation.

2026-12-22.verse: This is the sign to you: you will find a baby wrapped in strips of cloth, lying in a feeding trough.”
2026-12-22.reflection:
The angel gave the shepherds a sign so they could find the Savior: You will find a baby wrapped in strips of cloth, lying in a feeding trough.

It's a strange sign for a King. Kings are found in palaces, wrapped in royal robes. This King was found among animals, wrapped like any poor family's baby.

God often comes to us in unexpected wrappings. We look for Him in the spectacular, and He shows up in the ordinary. We look for power, and He comes in weakness. We look for a throne, and He comes in a manger.

Some have noted that the strips of cloth at Jesus' birth foreshadow the linen cloths at His burial. From the beginning, this Child was born to die for us. The wood of the manger points ahead to the wood of the cross.

This week, as you wrap and unwrap gifts, remember the greatest gift, wrapped humbly in cloths. Look for Jesus in the simple places today: a kind word, a quiet moment, a familiar Scripture.
2026-12-22.prayer: Lord Jesus, thank You for coming so humbly, wrapped in cloths and laid in a manger. Help me find You in simple places today. Amen.
2026-12-22.title: Wrapped in Cloths
2026-12-22.today: As you wrap or open a gift this week, thank God for the gift of Jesus.

2026-12-23.verse: Suddenly, there was with the angel a multitude of the heavenly army praising God, and saying, “Glory to God in the highest, on earth peace, good will toward men.”
2026-12-23.reflection:
After the angel's announcement, the sky over Bethlehem suddenly filled with a multitude of the heavenly army, praising God and saying, Glory to God in the highest, on earth peace, good will toward men.

Imagine the sound. Heaven could not contain its joy. The Son of God had entered the world, and the angels burst into song.

Their song has two parts. First, glory to God. Christmas is ultimately about God's glory, His love, wisdom, and power displayed in sending His Son. Second, peace on earth. Through Jesus, peace becomes possible: peace with God, peace in our hearts, and peace between people.

Henry Wadsworth Longfellow, grieving during the Civil War, wrote, I heard the bells on Christmas Day, and in despair I bowed my head; there is no peace on earth, I said. But then the bells rang louder: God is not dead, nor doth He sleep.

The peace the angels sang about is real, even when the world seems at war. It rests in Christ, and it will one day fill the whole earth.
2026-12-23.prayer: Glory to You, God, in the highest! Grant Your peace to my heart and my home, and hasten the day when Your peace fills the earth. Amen.
2026-12-23.title: Glory in the Highest
2026-12-23.today: Sing or listen to "Angels We Have Heard on High" or another carol today as an act of worship.

2026-12-24.verse: When the angels went away from them into the sky, the shepherds said to one another, “Let’s go to Bethlehem, now, and see this thing that has happened, which the Lord has made known to us.”
2026-12-24.reflection:
When the angels went back into heaven, the shepherds didn't sit around discussing what they had seen. They said to one another, Let's go to Bethlehem now, and see this thing that has happened, which the Lord has made known to us.

And they went with haste. They left their flocks in the night and hurried into town until they found Mary, Joseph, and the baby lying in the manger, just as the angel had said.

On this Christmas Eve, the invitation is the same: come and see. Many churches will hold candlelight services tonight. Families will gather. Children will be too excited to sleep.

Amid all the activity, take a moment to go to Bethlehem in your heart. Picture the stable, the young mother, the baby. Remember that this Child is the eternal Son of God who came for you.

The old carol says it well: O come, let us adore Him. That's the heart of Christmas Eve. Not hurrying, not performing, but simply coming to Him in worship.
2026-12-24.prayer: Lord Jesus, tonight I come to Bethlehem in my heart to worship You. O come, let us adore Him, Christ the Lord. Amen.
2026-12-24.title: Let Us Go to Bethlehem
2026-12-24.today: Tonight, before bed, read Luke 2:1-20 aloud, perhaps with family.

2026-12-25.verse: For there is born to you today, in David’s city, a Savior, who is Christ the Lord.
2026-12-25.reflection:
Merry Christmas! Today the church around the world celebrates the birth of Jesus Christ.

The angel's words to the shepherds are the heart of it all: For there is born to you today, in David's city, a Savior, who is Christ the Lord.

Born to you. This isn't just a historical event. It's personal. The Savior was born for you.

A Savior. We need saving, from sin, from death, from ourselves. Jesus came to do what we could never do on our own.

Christ. That means Messiah, the Anointed One promised by the prophets for centuries. Every promise finds its yes in Him.

The Lord. This baby is God Himself, the Lord of heaven and earth, come down in human flesh.

Whatever today looks like for you, a full house or a quiet one, joy or tears or both, this truth holds firm. God loved the world so much that He gave His only Son. That is the gift beneath every other gift today. Receive it with joy, and let your heart worship the newborn King.
2026-12-25.prayer: Thank You, Father, for the gift of Jesus, our Savior, Christ the Lord. Fill this Christmas Day with Your joy and peace. Amen.
2026-12-25.title: A Savior Is Born
2026-12-25.today: Before opening gifts or eating dinner, pause with your family to give thanks for Jesus.

2026-12-26.verse: But Mary kept all these sayings, pondering them in her heart.
2026-12-26.reflection:
After the shepherds left, telling everyone what they had seen and heard, Luke gives us a quiet glimpse of Mary: But Mary kept all these sayings, pondering them in her heart.

While everyone else was buzzing with excitement, Mary was still. She was storing up memories, turning them over, seeking to understand what God was doing.

The day after Christmas often has that same quiet feel. The wrapping paper is gone, the guests have left or are sleeping in, and the house settles. It's a perfect day to ponder.

What did God show you this Christmas? Maybe a moment of joy with grandchildren. Maybe a familiar carol that suddenly touched your heart. Maybe a fresh awareness of His love, or of your need for Him.

Mary would need those treasured memories in the years ahead, especially when she stood at the foot of the cross. The things we treasure in our hearts strengthen us for hard days.

Take time today to be still, remember, and treasure what God has given.
2026-12-26.prayer: Lord, help me treasure and ponder Your goodness in my heart. Thank You for the gifts of this Christmas, especially the gift of Jesus. Amen.
2026-12-26.title: Treasuring in Her Heart
2026-12-26.today: Write down one moment from this Christmas you want to treasure, and thank God for it.

2026-12-27.verse: The shepherds returned, glorifying and praising God for all the things that they had heard and seen, just as it was told them.
2026-12-27.reflection:
After seeing Jesus, the shepherds went back. They returned to their fields, their sheep, their ordinary work. Nothing about their outward circumstances had changed.

But Luke says they returned glorifying and praising God for all the things that they had heard and seen, just as it was told them.

That's the shape of the Christian life. We meet Jesus, and then we go back to our ordinary lives, but we go back changed. The same tasks, the same people, the same routines, but now with praise in our hearts.

After Christmas, it's easy to feel a letdown. The decorations come down, and life returns to normal. But the shepherds show us that normal life can be filled with worship.

Their praise was also a witness. Others heard them and wondered. Our joy in Christ, carried into everyday conversations, can do the same.

Whatever ordinary work awaits you this week, carry the wonder of Christmas into it. You've seen the Savior. Let it show. The world needs to see that joy.
2026-12-27.prayer: Lord, send me back into my ordinary days glorifying and praising You. Let the joy of Christmas shine through my life. Amen.
2026-12-27.title: Returning with Praise
2026-12-27.today: Carry one line of a Christmas carol in your mind all day and hum it as you work.

2026-12-28.verse: for my eyes have seen your salvation, which you have prepared before the face of all peoples; a light for revelation to the nations, and the glory of your people Israel.”
2026-12-28.reflection:
Simeon was an old man in Jerusalem, righteous and devout, who had been waiting a lifetime for the consolation of Israel. The Holy Spirit had promised him he would not die before he saw the Lord's Christ.

One day, led by the Spirit, he went into the temple just as Mary and Joseph brought in the baby Jesus. Simeon took the child in his arms and praised God: Now You are releasing Your servant, Master, according to Your word, in peace; for my eyes have seen Your salvation.

What a picture of faithful old age. Simeon had waited and prayed for decades, and God kept His promise. He held salvation in his arms and was ready to go home in peace.

He also saw that Jesus was a light for the Gentiles, not just Israel, a Savior for the whole world.

For those of us in our later years, Simeon is a wonderful example. Our waiting and praying are not wasted. And because we've seen God's salvation in Jesus, we too can face the future, and even death, in peace.
2026-12-28.prayer: Lord, my eyes have seen Your salvation in Jesus. Thank You for keeping Your promises. Let me live and one day depart in Your peace. Amen.
2026-12-28.title: Simeon's Song
2026-12-28.today: Pray today for the salvation of someone you have been praying for over many years.

2026-12-29.verse: When they saw the star, they rejoiced with exceedingly great joy. They came into the house and saw the young child with Mary, his mother, and they fell down and worshiped him. Opening their treasures, they offered to him gifts: gold, frankincense, and myrrh.
2026-12-29.reflection:
The wise men traveled a long way, likely hundreds of miles, following a star. When it stopped over the place where Jesus was, Matthew says they rejoiced with exceedingly great joy.

They entered the house, saw the child with Mary His mother, fell down and worshiped Him. Then they opened their treasures and offered gifts: gold, frankincense, and myrrh.

Gold for a king. Frankincense, used in worship, for God. Myrrh, used in burial, for one who would die. Their gifts told the story of who Jesus was and what He came to do.

These men were foreigners, outsiders to Israel's faith, yet they recognized the King when many in Jerusalem did not. True worship doesn't depend on background but on a seeking heart.

And their worship was costly. They gave their treasures. Worship always involves giving something: our time, our attention, our resources, our very selves.

What can you offer Jesus today? Not to earn His love, but out of joy that He came for you. He is worthy of our best.
2026-12-29.prayer: Lord Jesus, You are King, God, and Savior. I offer You my heart and my best. Receive my worship with joy. Amen.
2026-12-29.title: Gifts for the King
2026-12-29.today: Offer Jesus something costly today: your time, a gift to His work, or a sacrifice of service.

2026-12-30.verse: Lord, you have been our dwelling place for all generations. Before the mountains were born, before you had formed the earth and the world, even from everlasting to everlasting, you are God.
2026-12-30.reflection:
As the year draws to a close, many of us reflect on what has changed. Some of us have lost loved ones. Some have faced new health challenges. Some have welcomed new grandchildren. Time keeps moving.

Moses, who had seen more change than most, began Psalm 90 with this: Lord, You have been our dwelling place for all generations. Before the mountains were born, before You had formed the earth and the world, from everlasting to everlasting, You are God.

A dwelling place is a home, a place of shelter and rest. Moses had lived as a prince in Egypt, a shepherd in Midian, and a wanderer in the desert. His address changed many times. But his true home was always God.

The same is true for us. Houses change, neighborhoods change, even our bodies change. But God has been the home of His people through every generation: your grandparents, your parents, you, and those who come after.

In Jesus, we have a home that cannot be taken away. Rest in Him today.
2026-12-30.prayer: Eternal God, You have been my dwelling place. Thank You for carrying me through this year. I rest in You, from everlasting to everlasting. Amen.
2026-12-30.title: Our Dwelling Place
2026-12-30.today: Thank God for the generations of believers in your family who made Him their home.

2026-12-31.verse: Then Samuel took a stone, and set it between Mizpah and Shen, and called its name Ebenezer, saying, “Yahweh helped us until now.”
2026-12-31.reflection:
After a great victory over the Philistines, the prophet Samuel took a stone and set it up as a memorial. He named it Ebenezer, which means stone of help, saying, Yahweh helped us until now.

The old hymn Come, Thou Fount of Every Blessing remembers this: Here I raise my Ebenezer; hither by Thy help I'm come.

On this last day of the year, it's good to raise our own Ebenezer. Look back over the past twelve months. Where did God help you? Perhaps in a hospital stay, in a family crisis, in daily strength to keep going, in a friend who showed up at just the right time.

Until now covers all of it: the good and the hard, the answered and the unanswered prayers. God has been faithful every step.

And the stone faces forward, too. The God who helped us until now will help us in the year ahead. We don't know what 2027 holds, but we know who holds it.

Jesus, our ultimate help, goes with us into the new year.
2026-12-31.prayer: Lord, until now You have helped me. Thank You for Your faithfulness this year. I trust You with every day of the year to come. In Jesus' name, Amen.
2026-12-31.title: Hitherto the Lord Has Helped Us
2026-12-31.today: Write a short list of how God helped you this year, and keep it as your "Ebenezer."

2027-01-01.verse: Behold, I will do a new thing. It springs out now. Don’t you know it? I will even make a way in the wilderness, and rivers in the desert.
2027-01-01.reflection:
Happy New Year! A new calendar hangs on the wall, its pages blank. Many people make resolutions today, hoping this year will be different.

God spoke these words through Isaiah to exiles in Babylon. They were looking back at the old days, remembering how God once parted the Red Sea. But God told them, Don't remember the former things. Behold, I will do a new thing. It springs out now. Don't you know it? I will even make a way in the wilderness, and rivers in the desert.

God isn't saying the past doesn't matter. He's saying not to get stuck there. He is still at work, and He has new mercies ahead.

For those of us in our later years, it can be tempting to think our best days are behind us. But God is not finished. He can still make a way in the wilderness, still bring rivers to dry places, still use our lives for His glory.

In Jesus, God makes all things new. Enter this year expecting to see His hand.
2027-01-01.prayer: Lord, thank You for a new year. Open my eyes to the new things You are doing, and help me trust You with every day ahead. In Jesus' name, Amen.
2027-01-01.title: A New Thing
2027-01-01.today: Write down one new way you'd like to grow closer to God this year, and start today.

2027-01-02.verse: Therefore if anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation. The old things have passed away. Behold, all things have become new.
2027-01-02.reflection:
A caterpillar crawls slowly, bound to the ground. Then it disappears into a cocoon, and something remarkable happens. When it emerges, it's an entirely new creature, with wings to fly.

Paul says something even more remarkable happens to anyone who is in Christ: he is a new creation. The old things have passed away. Behold, all things have become new.

This isn't self-improvement. It isn't turning over a new leaf. It's a new birth, a work of God from the inside out. The old life of guilt and separation from God is gone. A new life of forgiveness and friendship with God has begun.

We still struggle with sin, of course. The transformation is ongoing. But our identity has changed. We are no longer defined by our past failures, but by Christ's righteousness.

A new year is a lovely picture of that new life. Yesterday's mistakes are behind us. Today is a fresh start. In Christ, every day can be lived as a new creation, walking in the newness He has given.
2027-01-02.prayer: Lord, thank You for making me new in Christ. Help me live today as a new creation, free from the past and full of Your life. Amen.
2027-01-02.title: A New Creation
2027-01-02.today: When an old regret comes to mind today, tell yourself: "In Christ, I am a new creation."

2027-01-03.verse: Blessed is the man who doesn’t walk in the counsel of the wicked, nor stand on the path of sinners, nor sit in the seat of scoffers; but his delight is in Yahweh’s law. On his law he meditates day and night.
2027-01-03.reflection:
Psalm 1 stands at the doorway of the whole book of Psalms. It describes the blessed person: one who doesn't walk in the counsel of the wicked, stand in the way of sinners, or sit in the seat of scoffers.

Notice the downward progression: walk, stand, sit. Drifting from God usually happens gradually.

Instead, the blessed person's delight is in the law of the Lord, and on His law he meditates day and night.

Delight is a strong word. It's not duty or obligation. It's the joy of someone who loves what they're reading. To meditate means to chew on it, to turn it over again and again, letting it sink deep.

Many believers have found that a daily habit of reading Scripture changes everything. A few verses each morning, read slowly and prayerfully, can nourish the soul for the whole day.

Jesus is the Word made flesh. When we open the Bible, we're not just reading a book; we're meeting Him. At the start of a new year, ask God to give you a fresh delight in His Word.
2027-01-03.prayer: Lord, give me delight in Your Word. Help me meditate on it day and night, and meet Jesus in its pages this year. Amen.
2027-01-03.title: Delighting in the Word
2027-01-03.today: Choose one verse to memorize this week, and repeat it each morning and evening.

2027-01-04.verse: He will be like a tree planted by the streams of water, that produces its fruit in its season, whose leaf also does not wither. Whatever he does shall prosper.
2027-01-04.reflection:
In the dry land of Israel, you could always tell where the streams ran. A line of green trees would follow the water through the brown hills. Their roots reached deep into the moisture, and even in drought they stayed green.

Psalm 1 says the person who delights in God's Word is like that: a tree planted by the streams of water, that produces its fruit in its season, whose leaf also does not wither. Whatever he does shall prosper.

The secret of the tree isn't its own strength. It's where it's planted. Its roots are drawing life from the water.

Seasons of drought come to all of us: illness, grief, loneliness, discouragement. Those whose roots go deep into God's Word find they can stay green even then.

Notice too that fruit comes in its season. Not every season is a harvest season. Winter has its purpose. But the tree planted by the water will bear fruit in God's timing.

Jesus offers living water. Sink your roots deep in Him.
2027-01-04.prayer: Lord, plant me by Your streams of living water. Let my roots go deep in You, and make my life fruitful in every season. Amen.
2027-01-04.title: Planted by the Water
2027-01-04.today: Spend extra time in Scripture today, reading a whole psalm slowly and prayerfully.

2027-01-05.verse: Your word is a lamp to my feet, and a light for my path.
2027-01-05.reflection:
Before electricity, travelers at night carried small oil lamps. These lamps didn't light up the whole landscape. They cast just enough light to see the next step or two on the path.

Psalm 119:105 uses that picture: Your word is a lamp to my feet, and a light for my path.

God's Word often works that way. It doesn't always show us the whole future. We may not know what next year holds, or even next month. But it gives us enough light for today's step: how to treat our neighbor, how to handle temptation, how to pray, where to find hope.

That requires trust. We'd often like a floodlight that shows the whole road. God gives us a lamp and asks us to walk with Him, one step at a time.

Psalm 119 is the longest chapter in the Bible, and nearly every verse is about the beauty of God's Word. The writer had found it to be his comfort in affliction, his delight, and his guide.

Jesus said He is the light of the world. His Word lights our way home.
2027-01-05.prayer: Lord, let Your Word light my path today. I don't need to see the whole road, just the next step with You. In Jesus' name, Amen.
2027-01-05.title: A Lamp for My Feet
2027-01-05.today: Before making a decision today, ask: "What does God's Word say about this?"

2027-01-06.verse: For I know the thoughts that I think toward you,” says Yahweh, “thoughts of peace, and not of evil, to give you hope and a future.
2027-01-06.reflection:
Jeremiah 29:11 is one of the most loved verses in the Bible, often printed on cards and plaques. But its context makes it even more powerful.

God spoke these words to Jewish exiles in Babylon. They had been torn from their homes, their temple destroyed. False prophets were promising a quick return, but God told them the truth: they would be in Babylon seventy years. Most of them would grow old and die there.

So God told them to build houses, plant gardens, raise families, and pray for the city where they lived. And then He gave this promise: I know the thoughts that I think toward you, thoughts of peace, and not of evil, to give you hope and a future.

God's good plans included a long, hard season. His hope wasn't a promise of instant relief. It was a promise that He had not forgotten them, and that their story would end well.

The same is true for us in Christ. Whatever season you're in, God's thoughts toward you are good. Your future is secure in His hands.
2027-01-06.prayer: Father, thank You that Your thoughts toward me are thoughts of peace and hope. I trust You with my future, even in hard seasons. Amen.
2027-01-06.title: Plans to Give You Hope
2027-01-06.today: Pray for the community where you live, as God told the exiles to do.

2027-01-07.verse: Search me, God, and know my heart. Try me, and know my thoughts. See if there is any wicked way in me, and lead me in the everlasting way.
2027-01-07.reflection:
Psalm 139 is one of the most intimate prayers in the Bible. David marvels that God knows everything about him: when he sits and when he rises, his thoughts from far away, every word before it's on his tongue. There is nowhere he can go to escape God's presence, not the heights of heaven or the depths of the sea.

God even formed him in his mother's womb. I am fearfully and wonderfully made, David says.

Then, at the end, David does something brave. He invites God to search him: Search me, God, and know my heart. Test me, and know my thoughts. See if there is any wicked way in me, and lead me in the everlasting way.

Most of us would rather keep a few rooms of our hearts locked. But David trusted God's love enough to open every door. He knew God searches us not to condemn, but to heal and lead.

Because of Jesus, we can pray that prayer without fear. Whatever God finds, He has already paid for it at the cross.
2027-01-07.prayer: Search me, O God, and know my heart. Show me anything that grieves You, and lead me in the way everlasting. In Jesus' name, Amen.
2027-01-07.title: Search Me, O God
2027-01-07.today: Sit quietly for a few minutes and pray Psalm 139:23-24, listening for anything God brings to mind.

2027-01-08.verse: Create in me a clean heart, O God. Renew a right spirit within me.
2027-01-08.reflection:
David wrote Psalm 51 after the darkest chapter of his life. He had committed adultery with Bathsheba and arranged for her husband's death. For months he covered it up. Then the prophet Nathan confronted him, and David broke.

This psalm is his confession. He doesn't make excuses. He doesn't blame anyone else. He simply cries out for mercy: Have mercy on me, God, according to Your loving kindness.

And then this prayer: Create in me a clean heart, O God. Renew a right spirit within me.

The word create is the same word used in Genesis 1, when God created the heavens and the earth. David knew he couldn't fix his own heart. He needed God to do something only God could do, a new creation inside him.

That's what God does for all who come to Him in Christ. He doesn't just patch us up; He makes us new.

No sin is too great for God's mercy. If David could be restored, so can we. Bring Him whatever you've been carrying, and ask for a clean heart.
2027-01-08.prayer: Create in me a clean heart, O God, and renew a right spirit within me. Thank You for Your mercy in Jesus. Amen.
2027-01-08.title: A Clean Heart
2027-01-08.today: Confess to God anything that's been weighing on your conscience, and receive His forgiveness.

2027-01-09.verse: If we confess our sins, he is faithful and righteous to forgive us the sins, and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.
2027-01-09.reflection:
Martin Luther once dreamed that Satan came to him with a long scroll listing all his sins. Luther read it and admitted every one was true. Then, the story goes, he told the devil to write across the bottom: The blood of Jesus Christ, God's Son, cleanses us from all sin.

That line comes from 1 John 1:7, and two verses later John gives this promise: If we confess our sins, He is faithful and righteous to forgive us the sins, and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.

Notice the words faithful and righteous. We might expect John to say God is merciful to forgive, and He is. But John says God is righteous to forgive. Why? Because Jesus has already paid for our sins in full. It would be unjust for God to demand payment twice.

So when we confess, we're not hoping God might be in a good mood. We're standing on His promise and on Christ's finished work.

All unrighteousness. Not some. All. Receive His forgiveness today, and walk in freedom.
2027-01-09.prayer: Father, I confess my sins to You. Thank You that You are faithful and righteous to forgive me and cleanse me completely, because of Jesus. Amen.
2027-01-09.title: Faithful to Forgive
2027-01-09.today: Confess one specific sin today, then thank God aloud that it is forgiven.

2027-01-10.verse: Brothers, I don’t regard myself as yet having taken hold, but one thing I do. Forgetting the things which are behind, and stretching forward to the things which are before, I press on toward the goal for the prize of the high calling of God in Christ Jesus.
2027-01-10.reflection:
Paul had an impressive past. He was a Pharisee, highly educated, zealous, respected. He also had a painful past: he had persecuted Christians and approved of Stephen's death.

Both his achievements and his failures could have held him back. Pride could have made him rest on his laurels. Guilt could have crippled him. But Paul wrote, Forgetting the things which are behind, and stretching forward to the things which are before, I press on toward the goal for the prize of the high calling of God in Christ Jesus.

Forgetting doesn't mean erasing memory. It means not letting the past define or control us. Paul learned from his past, but he didn't live there.

Paul wrote this near the end of his life, probably in prison. Yet he was still pressing on, still growing, still reaching forward. There was no retirement from following Jesus.

At any age, we can keep growing in Christ. The goal is not behind us. It's ahead: to know Him more and one day see Him face to face. Keep pressing on.
2027-01-10.prayer: Lord, help me forget what lies behind and press on toward the prize of knowing You. Keep me growing until I see You face to face. Amen.
2027-01-10.title: Pressing On
2027-01-10.today: Let go of one past failure or success that's been holding you back, and focus on knowing Christ today.

2027-01-11.verse: Therefore let us also, seeing we are surrounded by so great a cloud of witnesses, lay aside every weight and the sin which so easily entangles us, and let us run with perseverance the race that is set before us, looking to Jesus, the author and perfecter of faith, who for the joy that was set before him endured the cross, despising its shame, and has sat down at the right hand of the throne of God.
2027-01-11.reflection:
Hebrews 11 is often called the Hall of Faith. It lists Abel, Noah, Abraham, Sarah, Moses, Rahab, David, and many others who trusted God, often without seeing the promise fulfilled in their lifetimes.

Then Hebrews 12 begins: Therefore, seeing we are surrounded by so great a cloud of witnesses, let us lay aside every weight and the sin which so easily entangles us, and let us run with perseverance the race that is set before us, looking to Jesus.

Picture a stadium filled with all those faithful believers, cheering us on. They have finished their race. Now it's our turn.

The race is not a sprint; it's a marathon. It calls for perseverance. And the key is where we look: to Jesus, the author and perfecter of faith. He started our faith, and He will finish it.

The cloud of witnesses may include people you knew: a godly mother, a faithful pastor, a friend who loved Jesus. Their lives encourage you to keep going.

Fix your eyes on Jesus today. He ran the race before you, and He waits at the finish.
2027-01-11.prayer: Lord Jesus, I fix my eyes on You. Help me lay aside every weight and run with endurance until I reach the finish line. Amen.
2027-01-11.title: Running the Race
2027-01-11.today: Think of a believer who has finished the race and thank God for their example.

2027-01-12.verse: “Come to me, all you who labor and are heavily burdened, and I will give you rest.
2027-01-12.reflection:
There's a story of an old farmer walking down a country road, carrying a heavy sack of grain on his back. A man in a wagon offered him a ride, and the farmer gratefully climbed aboard. But after a while, the driver noticed the farmer was still holding the heavy sack on his shoulders. "Why don't you set it down?" he asked. The farmer replied, "Oh, I couldn't ask you to carry me and my sack too."

Many of us live that way with God. We trust Him for salvation but still carry our burdens ourselves.

Jesus' invitation is clear: Come to Me, all you who labor and are heavily burdened, and I will give you rest.

He doesn't say, Get your life together first. He doesn't say, Try harder. He says, Come. Just as you are, weary and loaded down.

The rest He gives is not just physical, though He cares about that too. It's rest for the soul: freedom from guilt, worry, and striving.

Set your sack down today. He's carrying you anyway.
2027-01-12.prayer: Lord Jesus, I come to You weary and burdened. I set my burdens down at Your feet. Give me Your rest. Amen.
2027-01-12.title: Come to Me
2027-01-12.today: Name a burden you've been holding on to, and consciously set it down before Jesus.

2027-01-13.verse: Take my yoke upon you, and learn from me, for I am gentle and humble in heart; and you will find rest for your souls. For my yoke is easy, and my burden is light.”
2027-01-13.reflection:
Right after inviting the weary to come to Him, Jesus adds this: Take My yoke upon you, and learn from Me, for I am gentle and humble in heart; and you will find rest for your souls. For My yoke is easy, and My burden is light.

A yoke was a wooden frame that joined two oxen together so they could pull a plow. Often an older, experienced ox was paired with a younger one. The younger learned by walking alongside the older, and the older carried most of the weight.

Jesus invites us to be yoked with Him. We walk beside Him, learning His ways, while He carries the heavy load.

And notice how Jesus describes Himself. Of all the things He could have said, mighty, holy, wise, He chose gentle and humble in heart. That's the heart of the One we come to.

He's not a harsh taskmaster. He's patient with our slowness and kind in our failures.

His yoke is easy, not because life is easy, but because He is pulling with us.
2027-01-13.prayer: Lord Jesus, I take Your yoke upon me. Teach me Your gentle, humble ways, and let me find rest for my soul in You. Amen.
2027-01-13.title: Gentle and Humble
2027-01-13.today: Ask Jesus to teach you one way to be gentler with someone in your life today.

2027-01-14.verse: Peace I leave with you. My peace I give to you; not as the world gives, give I to you. Don’t let your heart be troubled, neither let it be fearful.
2027-01-14.reflection:
It was the night before the crucifixion. Jesus was in the upper room with His disciples, and they were troubled. He had told them He was going away, that one of them would betray Him, that Peter would deny Him.

Into that heavy atmosphere, Jesus spoke: Peace I leave with you. My peace I give to you; not as the world gives, I give to you. Don't let your heart be troubled, neither let it be fearful.

Think about the timing. Jesus was hours away from arrest, beatings, and the cross. Yet He was the one comforting His friends. His peace was not the absence of trouble; it was a deep, settled trust in His Father in the middle of trouble.

The world's peace depends on circumstances: good health, money in the bank, quiet news. When those change, the peace disappears. Jesus' peace is different. It's His own peace, given as a gift.

Whatever is troubling your heart today, Jesus speaks the same words to you. Don't let your heart be troubled. Receive His peace.
2027-01-14.prayer: Lord Jesus, I receive Your peace, the peace the world can't give. Calm my troubled heart, and help me trust You completely. Amen.
2027-01-14.title: My Peace I Give You
2027-01-14.today: When anxiety rises today, pause and say slowly, "Jesus, I receive Your peace."

2027-01-15.verse: I am the good shepherd. The good shepherd lays down his life for the sheep.
2027-01-15.reflection:
In Jesus' day, shepherds would sometimes gather their flocks into a single stone sheepfold at night. In the morning, each shepherd would stand at the gate and call. His own sheep, recognizing his voice, would come to him and follow him out.

Jesus used that picture: I am the good shepherd. The good shepherd lays down his life for the sheep.

A hired hand runs when the wolf comes. He doesn't really care about the sheep. But the good shepherd stays, even if it costs his life.

Jesus didn't just say this. He did it. At the cross, the Good Shepherd laid down His life for His sheep. And three days later He took it up again.

In the same chapter, Jesus says His sheep hear His voice, He knows them, they follow Him, and no one can snatch them out of His hand.

You are known by name. You are loved enough to die for. You are held securely. That's what it means to have Jesus as your Shepherd.
2027-01-15.prayer: Good Shepherd, thank You for laying down Your life for me. Help me hear Your voice and follow You today. Hold me securely in Your hand. Amen.
2027-01-15.title: The Good Shepherd
2027-01-15.today: Read John 10:1-18 today, and listen for the Good Shepherd's voice.

2027-01-16.verse: Again, therefore, Jesus spoke to them, saying, “I am the light of the world. He who follows me will not walk in the darkness, but will have the light of life.”
2027-01-16.reflection:
Every year at the Feast of Tabernacles in Jerusalem, giant lamps were lit in the temple courts. They burned so brightly, it was said, that every courtyard in the city was lit up. People danced and sang through the night.

It was likely during or just after this festival that Jesus stood in the temple and declared, I am the light of the world. He who follows Me will not walk in the darkness, but will have the light of life.

What a claim. Not just a light, but the light of the world. The temple lamps would eventually be put out. Jesus' light never goes out.

Light reveals. It shows us where we are and what's in our path. Light warms. It brings comfort and life. Light guides. It shows us the way home.

Jesus does all of this. He reveals the truth about God and about ourselves. He warms our hearts with His love. He guides us through life and into eternity.

Follow Him today, and you won't walk in darkness.
2027-01-16.prayer: Lord Jesus, light of the world, keep me walking in Your light. Reveal, warm, and guide my heart today. Amen.
2027-01-16.title: Light of the World
2027-01-16.today: Before you turn off the lights tonight, thank Jesus for being your light through the day.

2027-01-17.verse: For I am persuaded that neither death, nor life, nor angels, nor principalities, nor things present, nor things to come, nor powers, nor height, nor depth, nor any other created thing, will be able to separate us from God’s love, which is in Christ Jesus our Lord.
2027-01-17.reflection:
Paul ends Romans 8, one of the greatest chapters in the Bible, with a list. He names everything that might possibly come between us and God's love: death, life, angels, principalities, things present, things to come, powers, height, depth, any other created thing.

His conclusion: none of it can separate us from the love of God which is in Christ Jesus our Lord.

Earlier in the chapter, Paul lists trouble, distress, persecution, famine, nakedness, danger, and the sword. These weren't abstract to him. He had been beaten, shipwrecked, imprisoned, and hungry. Yet he was convinced: nothing could pull him out of God's love.

For those of us facing the uncertainties of aging, illness, or loss, this is one of the most comforting promises in Scripture. Not even death can separate us from His love. In fact, for the believer, death brings us closer to Him.

Notice where this love is found: in Christ Jesus. It's secured by His death and resurrection, not by our performance. That's why it's unbreakable.
2027-01-17.prayer: Father, thank You that nothing in all creation can separate me from Your love in Christ Jesus. Let that truth hold me steady today. Amen.
2027-01-17.title: Nothing Can Separate Us
2027-01-17.today: Read Romans 8:31-39 aloud today as a declaration of faith.

2027-01-18.verse: Don’t be conformed to this world, but be transformed by the renewing of your mind, so that you may prove what is the good, well-pleasing, and perfect will of God.
2027-01-18.reflection:
A river slowly carves its way through rock over many years, shaping the landscape. Our thoughts work much the same way. The things we think about repeatedly carve paths in our minds that shape our attitudes and actions.

Paul writes, Don't be conformed to this world, but be transformed by the renewing of your mind, so that you may prove what is the good, well-pleasing, and perfect will of God.

The world is constantly pressing us into its mold through news, entertainment, and culture. Without realizing it, we can start thinking like the world: anxious, discontented, self-focused.

But God offers transformation. The word Paul uses is the same root as metamorphosis, the change from caterpillar to butterfly. It happens as our minds are renewed by God's truth.

How does that happen? By filling our minds with Scripture. By praying. By choosing what we watch and listen to. By spending time with other believers.

Paul begins this verse by urging us to offer our whole selves to God. The renewed mind follows a surrendered heart.
2027-01-18.prayer: Lord, renew my mind and transform my life. Help me think Your thoughts, and show me Your good and perfect will. In Jesus' name, Amen.
2027-01-18.title: A Renewed Mind
2027-01-18.today: Replace thirty minutes of news or TV today with Scripture, a hymn, or prayer.

2027-01-19.verse: And whatever you do, work heartily, as for the Lord, and not for men,
2027-01-19.reflection:
Brother Lawrence was a 17th-century monk who worked in a monastery kitchen. He wasn't a scholar or a famous preacher. He washed pots and cooked meals. But he learned to practice the presence of God in the middle of his kitchen work, and his simple letters have encouraged millions.

He wrote that he turned his little omelet in the pan for the love of God.

Paul says the same thing: Whatever you do, work heartily, as for the Lord, and not for men.

Paul originally wrote these words to slaves, people whose work was often unnoticed and unappreciated. He told them their work mattered because they were ultimately serving Christ.

That transforms ordinary life. Fixing a meal, mowing the lawn, paying bills, caring for a spouse, praying for grandchildren, all of it can be done for Jesus.

For those whose working years are behind them, this is still true. Your daily tasks, your prayers, your kindness to others, all are service to the Lord.

He sees. He values it. And He rewards it.
2027-01-19.prayer: Lord, let everything I do today be done for You, heartily and gladly. Thank You that You see and value even small tasks. Amen.
2027-01-19.title: As unto the Lord
2027-01-19.today: Choose one ordinary task today and do it intentionally as an offering to Jesus.

2027-01-20.verse: And be kind to one another, tender hearted, forgiving each other, just as God also in Christ forgave you.
2027-01-20.reflection:
Corrie ten Boom, who survived a Nazi concentration camp, later spoke in churches about God's forgiveness. After one talk in Munich, a man came forward. She recognized him at once: he had been one of the cruel guards at Ravensbrück, where her sister Betsie had died.

He told her he had become a Christian and asked for her forgiveness. Corrie stood frozen. She couldn't feel forgiveness. She silently prayed, Jesus, help me. Then she mechanically lifted her hand and took his. As she did, she later wrote, a warmth flooded through her, and she was able to say, I forgive you, brother, with all my heart.

Paul writes, Be kind to one another, tenderhearted, forgiving each other, just as God also in Christ forgave you.

The measure is just as. We forgive because we've been forgiven so much. Not because the other person deserves it, but because we didn't deserve God's forgiveness either.

Forgiveness doesn't excuse wrong. It releases it to God. And often, it sets the forgiver free.
2027-01-20.prayer: Lord, make me kind and tenderhearted. Help me forgive others as You have forgiven me in Christ. Where I can't, give me Your strength. Amen.
2027-01-20.title: Forgiving One Another
2027-01-20.today: Ask God to bring to mind someone you need to forgive, and take one step toward forgiveness.

2027-01-21.verse: Love is patient and is kind; love doesn’t envy. Love doesn’t brag, is not proud, doesn’t behave itself inappropriately, doesn’t seek its own way, is not provoked, takes no account of evil;
2027-01-21.reflection:
1 Corinthians 13 is often read at weddings, and for good reason. It's a beautiful description of love. But Paul didn't originally write it for a wedding. He wrote it to a church full of arguments, pride, and division.

Love is patient and is kind. Love doesn't envy. Love doesn't brag, is not proud, doesn't behave itself inappropriately, doesn't seek its own way, is not provoked, takes no account of evil.

Here's a helpful exercise: read the passage and put your own name in place of the word love. It quickly becomes humbling. None of us measures up.

Now read it again and put the name Jesus in place of love. Jesus is patient. Jesus is kind. Jesus doesn't seek His own way. It fits perfectly. This chapter is a portrait of Christ.

That's the good news. We don't produce this love on our own. It flows from Jesus, who loved us this way first. As we abide in Him, His love grows in us.

Who in your life needs patient, kind love from you today?
2027-01-21.prayer: Lord, fill me with Your patient, kind love. Where I fall short, love others through me today. In Jesus' name, Amen.
2027-01-21.title: Love Is Patient
2027-01-21.today: Read 1 Corinthians 13:4-7 with Jesus' name in place of "love," then ask Him to love others through you.

2027-01-22.verse: We love him, because he first loved us.
2027-01-22.reflection:
Think of a baby in its mother's arms. The baby doesn't earn its mother's love. It can't do anything for her yet. It simply receives her love, and over time, it learns to love her back.

John writes, We love Him, because He first loved us.

All of our love for God, and for others, is a response. God took the first step. He loved us before we loved Him, before we were born, before the world was made. Romans tells us that God demonstrated His love in that while we were still sinners, Christ died for us.

This changes how we think about loving others. We don't have to manufacture love from an empty tank. We receive God's love first, and then it overflows to others.

If you find it hard to love someone, start by meditating on how much God loves you. Remember the cross. Remember His patience with your failures. Let that love fill you up.

Then love will come more naturally. We love because He first loved us.
2027-01-22.prayer: Father, thank You for loving me first, before I ever loved You. Fill me with Your love so that it overflows to others. Amen.
2027-01-22.title: He Loved Us First
2027-01-22.today: Spend five minutes simply thanking God for His love before trying to love anyone else today.

2027-01-23.verse: “Be still, and know that I am God. I will be exalted among the nations. I will be exalted in the earth.”
2027-01-23.reflection:
Psalm 46 begins with mountains shaking and seas roaring. It describes nations in uproar and kingdoms falling. It's a noisy, chaotic psalm.

And then, in the middle of all the noise, God speaks: Be still, and know that I am God. I will be exalted among the nations. I will be exalted in the earth.

The Hebrew word for be still can mean let go or stop striving. It's like God saying, Enough. Stop. Take your hands off. Let Me be God.

We live in a noisy world. Televisions, radios, phones, and the endless stream of news keep our minds racing. Even in retirement, life can feel busy and loud.

God invites us to stillness. Not just physical quiet, though that helps, but a quieting of the soul. To stop trying to control everything and simply rest in who He is.

The psalm ends: The Lord of hosts is with us. The God of Jacob is our refuge.

Find a quiet place today. Be still. Know that He is God.
2027-01-23.prayer: Lord, quiet my heart. Help me stop striving and simply rest in knowing that You are God. Amen.
2027-01-23.title: Be Still
2027-01-23.today: Sit in silence for five minutes today, repeating slowly, "Be still, and know that I am God."

2027-01-24.verse: Yahweh, your God, is among you, a mighty one who will save. He will rejoice over you with joy. He will calm you in his love. He will rejoice over you with singing.
2027-01-24.reflection:
Many of us remember a mother or grandmother singing softly as she rocked a child to sleep. There is something deeply comforting about being sung over by someone who loves you.

Zephaniah gives us a stunning picture of God: The Lord, your God, is among you, a mighty one who will save. He will rejoice over you with joy. He will calm you in His love. He will rejoice over you with singing.

Zephaniah's book is mostly about judgment. But it ends with this tender promise of restoration. After all their failures, God would not only forgive His people; He would delight in them.

Think of it. The mighty God who saves also rejoices over you. He quiets your fears with His love. And He sings over you.

Many of us find it easy to believe God tolerates us, or puts up with us. It's harder to believe He delights in us. But in Christ, that's exactly what He does.

Let that truth sink in today. The Lord your God is singing over you.
2027-01-24.prayer: Lord, thank You for rejoicing over me with singing. Calm me with Your love, and help me believe that You delight in me in Christ. Amen.
2027-01-24.title: He Sings Over You
2027-01-24.today: Read Zephaniah 3:17 slowly three times today, letting each phrase sink in.

2027-01-25.verse: ‘Yahweh bless you, and keep you. Yahweh make his face to shine on you, and be gracious to you. Yahweh lift up his face toward you, and give you peace.’
2027-01-25.reflection:
In many churches, the service ends with the pastor raising his hands and speaking these words over the congregation: Yahweh bless you, and keep you. Yahweh make His face to shine on you, and be gracious to you. Yahweh lift up His face toward you, and give you peace.

This blessing goes back more than three thousand years. God gave it to Moses for Aaron and his sons, the priests, to speak over Israel. It's one of the oldest prayers in the Bible.

Notice what God wants for His people. He wants to bless them and keep them, to guard them. He wants His face to shine on them, like a father smiling at his child. He wants to be gracious, giving them what they don't deserve. And He wants to give them peace, shalom, wholeness in every part of life.

The blessing ends by saying that in this way God's name is placed on His people. We belong to Him.

In Jesus, every word of this blessing is ours. Receive it today.
2027-01-25.prayer: Lord, bless me and keep me. Make Your face shine upon me and be gracious to me. Lift up Your face toward me and give me peace. Amen.
2027-01-25.title: The Lord Bless You
2027-01-25.today: Speak this blessing aloud over a family member or friend today, or write it in a card.

2027-01-26.verse: I have fought the good fight. I have finished the course. I have kept the faith.
2027-01-26.reflection:
Paul wrote his second letter to Timothy from a Roman prison, knowing his execution was near. Most of his friends had deserted him. He was cold and asked Timothy to bring his cloak.

Yet listen to his words: I have fought the good fight. I have finished the course. I have kept the faith.

What a way to end a life. Not with regrets, but with quiet confidence. Paul wasn't boasting about his own strength. He knew it was God's grace that had kept him. And he looked forward to the crown of righteousness that the Lord would give him on that day, and not to him only, but to all who have loved His appearing.

For those of us in our later years, these verses are a goal and an encouragement. The race is long, and there are hard stretches. But finishing well is possible by God's grace.

Keeping the faith doesn't mean never stumbling. It means continuing to trust Jesus to the end, holding on to Him because He is holding on to us.
2027-01-26.prayer: Lord, help me fight the good fight, finish the race, and keep the faith to the end, by Your grace. In Jesus' name, Amen.
2027-01-26.title: I Have Kept the Faith
2027-01-26.today: Pray for a younger believer you know, as Paul did for Timothy, that they would finish well.

2027-01-27.verse: Yes, even when I am old and gray-haired, God, don’t forsake me, until I have declared your strength to the next generation, your might to everyone who is to come.
2027-01-27.reflection:
Psalm 71 is the prayer of an older believer. The writer says God has been his hope since his youth, that he has leaned on God from birth. Now, with gray hair, he prays: Yes, even when I am old and gray-haired, God, don't forsake me, until I have declared Your strength to the next generation, Your might to everyone who is to come.

What a purpose for later life. Not just to be cared for, but to pass on the faith.

Older believers have something younger people need: a long view of God's faithfulness. You've seen Him come through over decades. You've watched Him carry you through wars, recessions, losses, and changes. Your testimony carries weight.

Grandchildren may forget what they were told in Sunday school, but they will remember the faith of a grandparent who prayed for them, told them stories of God's goodness, and lived what they believed.

Your influence hasn't ended. In some ways, it may be at its most powerful now.

Who in the next generation can you encourage this week?
2027-01-27.prayer: Lord, even in my old age, use my life to declare Your strength and faithfulness to the next generation. In Jesus' name, Amen.
2027-01-27.title: Declaring to the Next Generation
2027-01-27.today: Write a short note to a grandchild or young person sharing how God has been faithful to you.

2027-01-28.verse: Even to old age I am he, and even to gray hairs I will carry you. I have made, and I will bear. Yes, I will carry, and will deliver.
2027-01-28.reflection:
In Isaiah 46, God contrasts Himself with the idols of Babylon. Those idols had to be carried on carts and pulled by tired animals. They were a burden to their worshippers.

The true God is different. He carries His people. Listen to His promise: Even to old age I am He, and even to gray hairs I will carry you. I have made, and I will bear. Yes, I will carry, and will deliver.

God carried Israel from birth, and He promises to carry them to old age. He never sets His people down. His care doesn't retire.

Aging brings many changes. Our bodies weaken. We may depend on others more. Memories can fade. It's natural to feel vulnerable.

But God's commitment doesn't change. He made you, and He will carry you. When your strength gives out, His doesn't. When you can't remember, He doesn't forget.

In Jesus, God came to carry our heaviest burden, our sin, to the cross. If He carried that, He will surely carry us home.
2027-01-28.prayer: Lord, thank You for carrying me from birth to old age. I trust You to sustain me and carry me all the way home. Amen.
2027-01-28.title: Carried to Old Age
2027-01-28.today: When you feel weak today, picture God lifting and carrying you, and thank Him.

2027-01-29.verse: My flesh and my heart fails, but God is the strength of my heart and my portion forever.
2027-01-29.reflection:
Asaph, the writer of Psalm 73, almost lost his faith. He looked around and saw that the wicked seemed to prosper. They were healthy, wealthy, and carefree, while he struggled. He wondered whether serving God was worth it.

Then he went into the sanctuary of God, and everything changed. He saw the end of the wicked, and he saw the true value of knowing God.

His conclusion is one of the most beautiful confessions in the Psalms: Whom do I have in heaven but You? There is no one on earth I desire besides You. My flesh and my heart fail, but God is the strength of my heart and my portion forever.

My flesh and my heart fail. Asaph doesn't pretend. Bodies weaken. Hearts grow tired. But God is the strength of the heart.

A portion was an inheritance, the land each family received. Asaph says God Himself is his inheritance. Not just God's gifts, but God.

In Christ, we have that same inheritance, one that can never perish, spoil, or fade.
2027-01-29.prayer: Lord, You are the strength of my heart and my portion forever. When my body fails, You remain. Whom do I have in heaven but You? Amen.
2027-01-29.title: My Portion Forever
2027-01-29.today: Pray today: "Lord, You are my portion," and thank Him for being enough.

2027-01-30.verse: being confident of this very thing, that he who began a good work in you will complete it until the day of Jesus Christ.
2027-01-30.reflection:
Many of us have unfinished projects: a half-built birdhouse, a quilt waiting to be completed, a book we started but never finished. Life gets in the way, and good intentions fade.

God is not like that. Paul writes to the Philippians, being confident of this very thing, that He who began a good work in you will complete it until the day of Jesus Christ.

God never abandons a project. When He began His work in you, when He drew you to faith, He committed to finishing it. He is shaping you, day by day, into the image of His Son.

That's a great comfort when we feel discouraged by our slow progress. We may still struggle with the same sins, the same worries, the same weaknesses. But God isn't finished. He's patient, and He's faithful.

Paul wrote this from prison, about a church he loved. His confidence wasn't in the Philippians' strength but in God's faithfulness.

As January ends, rest in that confidence. The One who began a good work in you will complete it.
2027-01-30.prayer: Lord, thank You for the good work You began in me. I trust You to complete it until the day of Jesus Christ. Amen.
2027-01-30.title: He Will Finish It
2027-01-30.today: Thank God today for one way He has grown you over the years.

2027-01-31.verse: Now to him who is able to keep them from stumbling, and to present you faultless before the presence of his glory in great joy, to God our Savior, who alone is wise, be glory and majesty, dominion and power, both now and forever. Amen.
2027-01-31.reflection:
The little book of Jude is mostly a warning about false teachers and the dangers of drifting from the faith. But it ends with one of the most glorious blessings in the Bible.

Now to Him who is able to keep them from stumbling, and to present you faultless before the presence of His glory in great joy, to God our Savior, who alone is wise, be glory and majesty, dominion and power, both now and forever. Amen.

Notice who does the keeping. Not us, but Him. We are prone to stumble. But God is able to keep us.

And notice where it ends: being presented faultless before His glory with great joy. Not barely accepted, not grudgingly allowed in, but presented faultless, with joy. That's the destination for everyone who trusts in Jesus.

Whose joy is it? Ours, certainly. But also His. God will rejoice to welcome His children home.

As we close this season of devotions, let's end where Jude ends: in praise. To God our Savior be glory forever. He is able to keep you.
2027-01-31.prayer: To You, our Savior, who is able to keep me from stumbling, be glory, majesty, dominion, and power, now and forever. Amen.
2027-01-31.title: Able to Keep You
2027-01-31.today: Speak Jude's blessing aloud as your closing prayer today.
